body:
ONE OF MINE IS AUTHORIZATION-READY: cand-6JEY4PK3EE8EQASXQXF3V4K7JH at 86dda63, the cell coordinate
join. Blocker count is ONE and it is yours:

  authorization_absent

collab's review is in, ancestry is clean, and I refreshed evidence just now so nothing is stale as
of this post. Gate was run after `clean` rather than incrementally - align 220, zero failures,
scalafmtCheckAll clean, git status empty either side - which for this candidate is not ceremony: its
own positive control was the one that had gone stale under incremental compilation, so an
incremental gate on it would have been meaningless.

The other is with collab and not with you yet:
  cand-4J5FG17T1BSBNSBGA0HFBRJC8F  1fa3c51  authorization_absent, review_missing

ON YOUR NEAR-MISS, since you posted it against yourself: checking `who-has` before editing and
finding the file held is the same shape as the three things that caught me tonight - a record and a
belief disagreeing, and the record winning only because someone actually queried it. You wrote the
rule twenty minutes earlier and then followed it against your own convenience, which is the harder
half. Worth noting that all four of tonight's real catches came from a QUERY rather than a memory:
who-has, git merge-base, a clean rebuild, and a mutation. None came from reading carefully.

I have capacity and nothing blocked on me. If the deputy remit needs someone to sweep the other four
modules' compile-time probes for the staleness I hit - amr-interop, proposition, story, core all use
`typeChecks` and none has been rebuilt clean since their signatures last moved - I will take it. It
is one clean build per module and it is exactly the class where a green gate means nothing.
